utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Okay, good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Excuse me. It's okay? Do you hear me? I said good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen, and I am sorry for the delay we have suffered. I hope nobody is really harmed because of that. Please if the registrar will call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-03-66-PT, the Prosecutor versus Fatmir Limaj, Haradin Bala and Isak Musliu.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Can we have the appearances, please, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, good afternoon. For the Prosecution, Alex Whiting, along with Mr. Colin Black, and Mr. Bill Smith.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Whiting. For the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: If it please Your Honour, Karim Khan for Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GASHI
utterances.text: Tome Gashi, for Haradin Bala.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, Peter Murphy also for Haradin Bala.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Steven Powles for Isak Musliu.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Thank you. I've been informed of what's been going on lately in the case in order to be of some use in this meeting -- is there any problem? And I'm glad to know that the disclosure is working at a pace which could be considered good with a few exceptions. I have been told that the proposition of 13 92 bis article of the witnesses of the Prosecution haven't been answered by the counsels for the accused, but I don't know if it has been transmitted to them very recently, they have still time to -- okay, don't tell me anything. I see by your face that you agree with my assumption. The second point relates to -- in relation with the disclosure matters is the -- it seems to me there is not complete accordance between the Prosecution and the counsels about the possibility of cooperating in this last one - I mean the counsels for the accused - in tracing and devising what could be the points or the methods even of exculpatory evidence that could be included in the Prosecutor's papers. I think they had offered you to give to the Office of the Prosecution an answer about how to devise -- how to get, to recover, in other words, whatever could be of exculpatory evidence for your clients. So I would encourage you to try to find a solution to that, and then that you find it agreeable for you to do that. Well, I hope that could be done in order to push a little bit the expeditiousness of the -- and the resolution of the case. Another question that I would like to slightly mention only is that the Prosecution has asked for protective measures for eight extra witnesses. The question has been to -- is going to be considered by the Court. And of course, you know about this petition being made by the Prosecution. There's another point that sometimes is helpful, is the agreement on certain facts between the parties. And I would like to encourage you to try to agree on these points as much as possible, because without being any harm for anybody of the accused, it's at the same time another possibility to arrive to the disposal of the case sooner. I had also been told that yesterday in the 65 ter meeting there was given an appraisal about the moments at which the case could be -- go to trial. The information I had got is somehow a little bit contradictory in the sense that even if the Prosecution - and correct me if I am not right - has suggested they could be able to present their -- his or her brief by the end of January. At the same time, it was made a suggestion that the possibility of asking for a new amendment of the indictment. In this case that could determine on the side of the -- of the counsels for the accused to have to ask for another motion, and that it wouldn't be possible at this -- in this consensus to go to -- to take the case to court six weeks after the presentation of the brief by the Prosecution. So I tried to encourage also the Prosecution to do its best -- her best in the -- in dealing with this matter, because -- because it would be good for the expeditious way in which the case should be dealt with. I don't think there is, unless you have some suggestions, any other matter that could be of merit to be considered now at this moment and at this meeting. Please, if you have some other matters that would you like to bring about, please do now. The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, I would just like to address the Court's final point about the amended indictment, because I can understand that that could cause some concern to the Court, with respect to the schedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: I'm hearing -- pardon me?

utterances.speaker: MR. GASHI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't have translation into Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Is it now working? Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: I am hearing you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I think it was the Albanian translation which wasn't working, but it is now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: That is probably the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'll start again. I'll just address the Court's final point about an amend indictment, because I can understand that that might cause the Court some concern with regard to the schedule. It is our intention to seek leave from the Chamber to amend the indictment, and we will do that, I expect, within the next couple of weeks. I do not, however, believe that this should cause any significant delay in the scheduling. We will not be expanding the factual basis of the indictment, with the exception of an addition of one single crime. What we'll be doing is simply elaborating and adding to the legal basis in the indictment, and specifically adding a joint criminal enterprise charge. Now, of course, I understand that that triggers the possibility of a new round of preliminary motions by the Defence; however, I don't -- I do not think that that should delay the proceedings. I think that that can be done in conjunction with the continued disclosure and preparation for trial. It's certainly the Prosecution's intention, even with an amended indictment, to submit its pre-trial brief by the end of January. It is also the Prosecution's intention to seek every way possible to expedite disclosure and to cooperate and reach agreement on issues such as 92 bis and agreed facts so that this case can go to trial as quickly as possible. That is our priority, it remains our priority, and it will continue to be our priority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Whiting. I am very glad to hear that you -- your intentions are not to delay at all the arrival to the court hearing of the case. I hope you can maintain your promise and without problems for the counsels of the accused. If you don't have any other suggestions, I would like to ask -- you have. Please, tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, on behalf of Mr. Musliu, there is one matter, if I may, that I would like to raise this afternoon. Your Honour will see that today I appear in court without the assistance of lead counsel. Mr. Musliu is minded to instruct a Mr. Klaus Kirchner, a member of the bar in Germany, to represent him as lead counsel. Mr. Kirchner today sits in the public gallery observing these proceedings. I understand that Mr. Kirchner was removed initially from the Rule 45 list of eligible counsel by the -- a decision of the Registrar. He thereafter appealed that decision to the President, and Your Honour may be aware that the President issued a decision on the 21st of October, on the question of the assignment of Defence counsel. In essence, the President concluded that Mr. Kirchner should resubmit various documents to the Registrar for reconsideration of his application, firstly to be on the Rule 45 list, and thereafter Mr. Musliu's representative as lead counsel. I am informed that Mr. Kirchner has indeed already submitted such documents to the Registry, and I would respectfully request that such reconsideration take place as a matter of urgency so that the question of Mr. Musliu's representation can be finalised and preparation -- or the continued preparation of his defence can continue in earnest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Powles. I wonder if the representation of the Registrar can give us any information about the situation. Has this document been returned to the Office of the Registrar?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Well, I hope that -- no, don't worry. Sit down. What you are asking for can be dealt with with the -- with the Office of the Registrar. So I cannot -- Some of the other counsel would like to say some problems?

utterances.speaker: MR. GASHI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm Tome Gashi for Mr. Bala. In the earlier Status Conference, the latest one, the Prosecutor required -- can you hear me in English -- to give us the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear me in English now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GASHI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But up to now, the material has not been received by us, in particular, the material regarding the imprisonment of Mr. Murtezi, for whom the other side has given up the indictment or has abandoned the indictment. We don't know anything about the material, and we think that you should exercise your influence with the Prosecution so that the material be given over, be handed over in accordance with regulation 68, because we regard this as exculpatory material, all material which has to do with the imprisonment of Mr. Murtezi. We don't know if there is any more exculpatory material which could be transmitted to our side at all. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gashi. Well, I wondered if you had already asked - I suppose you have - the Prosecutor about getting this material you are finally lacking, about Mr. Murtezi being included in the first indictment and later on being released. You have. Well, that could be possible for you to apply to the -- to make arrangement with the Prosecution to get this information and the document required. I mean, it could be normally available for --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, this -- this issue came up at the last Status Conference and 65 ter Conference. Following that conference, the Prosecution reviewed all of the material related to the arrest of Mr. Murtezi and disclosed all of the information that was Rule 68 for these accused promptly, I am happy to re-send that information, but it has already been done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Okay. So you have some answer that could be perhaps satisfactory for you. Any other subjects that you would like to raise now? Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, just in relation to that last point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Perhaps the area of dispute relates to the definition of "exculpatory evidence."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: The concern of the Defence, of course, is having sight of the evidence that led the Prosecution to release Mr. Murtezi and not only release him but to amend the indictment so that his name was removed. It appears my learned friend is simply confining himself to the evidence which may, strictly speaking, seem to mitigate or otherwise show a defence in relation to my particular client. It's my submission that exculpatory evidence is wider than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Because if a doubt has been cast upon evidence in relation to part of the Prosecution case, what we want to know is whether or not those same witnesses that were unreliable and led to the withdrawal of Mr. Murtezi's case are witnesses against my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: That's the specific issue that I would like clarification upon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Well, thank you, Mr. Khan. I think that the release of Mr. Murtezi was on the basis that he wasn't the right person that was being searched. But I would say that every precedent that is included in the case that could be of any, let's say, favourable -- favour for the accused could be submitted to you. So I suppose if you ask for it, you will get this possibility. And I think in any case, you can make a motion to the Court in this sense and to even study about the possibilities that -- I primarily believe that it will be possible for you to get this information, but we'll try to see whatever this is, if this is really necessary for you because it's exculpatory value for your -- for your client. So if you don't have any other questions to submit to me now, I will refer to the persons of the accused. Mr. Limaj, please, would you stand up. Do you understand me well in a language you understand yourself? And the proceedings that have been going on so far, you have understood everything that has been translated to your satisfaction, in a language that you understand? THE ACCUSED LIMAJ: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Okay. I would like to know if you have any other suggestions to -- well, to see -- to review, to allow you the possibility of reviewing the state of your case and if you have any other issue to raise in spite of the -- besides those that have been raised by your -- your counsel. THE ACCUSED LIMAJ: [Interpretation] I think my lawyer said everything which had to be said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Okay. THE ACCUSED LIMAJ: [Interpretation] Because I'm in the final stage of proceedings here. We've -- there's been a long time that we haven't had an opportunity to say what we wanted to say, and now we're in the final phase and the procedures I think will be respected, and we will conduct everything through our counsel, because up to now no opportunity has been given to us to express our opinions, and I hope that we will have an opportunity now to express our views on the issue. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Well, exactly this kind of a Status Conference are the moment for you to be heard about whatever complaint or whatever matter you would like to. More specifically, I would like to ask you about the question of your situation and your health and your mental and physical condition. You are feeling well treated and you have any problems within your stay in the Detention Unit related to your health? THE ACCUSED LIMAJ: [Interpretation] As to my personal situation, I'm fine. My health is all right. I don't have any health problems. And treatment, as I said previously, I'm extremely satisfied with the treatment I'm receiving. So I don't have anything to complain about with regard to my personal situation. Whereas, other problems about the procedures here in the trial, I think my lawyer will raise the issues. One of the major problems that I'm having, that I would like to mention or request is that I haven't been given an opportunity to express my views directly with regard to my request for provisional release. I think this is part of the procedure, and I think I should have an opportunity to express myself directly with arguments with regard to provisional release and with regard to the refusal thereof.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Limaj. You may sit down. The problem of your provisional release, as you may know well - I suppose your counsel has informed you about - has been denied at the level of the Trial Court and has been subjected to a -- an appeal which is now to be decided by the -- the appealing section of the Tribunal. That's the most I can tell you, because it's out of my power now to take a decision on this matter. Mr. Bala, please. Do you have any suggestions or any issue you would like to raise about your case or the way your case is being handled and -- that I could in some way be able to -- to correct, if necessary? THE ACCUSED BALA: [Interpretation] No, I have nothing special to say, and I think what I do have to say will be said by my legal representative, my lawyer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: In relation with your health, you had presented in the past some problems, I remember, and I have read about the -- the report given by the doctor that attended, I mean that took care of you. Do you have any other problems now? You are well cared for? Do you feel all right? THE ACCUSED BALA: [Interpretation] Everything is fine. I'm being very well treated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Okay. I remember that the doctor said that you could help if you stopped smoking, so probably that will be something that will contribute to your well-being. Okay. Please sit down. And please, Mr. Musliu, will you please -- do you have any matter you would like to bring to the attention of the -- of the Court on the disposal of your case? THE GUARD: The microphone doesn't work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: It doesn't work? THE ACCUSED MUSLIU: [Interpretation] Thank you that you've given me an opportunity to talk. I agree with everything what you said up to now, and I have nothing to add for the moment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Well, my problem now is you have been understanding whatever has been said during this meeting, in a language you could understand, or you have been deprived of the translation? THE ACCUSED MUSLIU: [Interpretation] Oh, I've understood everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Okay. About your health now, a point you would like to remark about that? THE ACCUSED MUSLIU: [Interpretation] My health is fine, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Okay. You may sit down. I have been informed also about a matter which I would like to comment on. It is the fact that the accused are brought whenever they have to get out from the Detention Unit and to come here to the Tribunal, they are brought handcuffed and blindfolded. I know your complaints about this situation. I want you to know that the decision on this aspect of your treatment is not completely to the power of this Tribunal, of this Court, because you are treated like that in -- by the local police, the Dutch police, which understands that this is necessary for you attending to the criteria that you may be subjected to this kind of treatment. I am afraid that is the case. Nevertheless, I would endeavour to the Registrar to take some steps with the local police - that's the police of the Netherlands - to see if that situation could be eased without any problem. So that is the most I can tell you about that. I know that a short statement about the situation has been distributed, if not to you at least to your counsels. So I think it would be helpful and we'll try to get some better situation for you in the future. I don't think is there any other question that you would like to bring about now? Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, just one matter arising out of that: It's right to say that every administrative decision must be judicially reviewable and the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: -- decision regarding the conditions of transit is a matter of great concern to my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I would ask that, as you've already said, that the matter be raised with the Registrar, but more particularly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: -- if a favourable decision is not forthcoming, if the conditions are not different on the next occasion, I would request that the parties be notified in advance, because I can say that if they do not change, it may be much more difficult for the accused to agree to come here. So it is a matter of great concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Khan. I understand what you mean. But if you are seeking an administrative review or a judicial review of the administrative decisions - please, sit down - you have to respect that. I mean, you are referring to the way the -- your client and the clients of the other counsels are being treated. You have to apply to the Dutch administration or the Dutch court. I suppose they -- I mean, completely sure that we have means to make repair and to have the judicial decision about all this. It's the most I can say about that. Well, if not --

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. Perhaps I didn't make myself clear. My point was different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Oh, your point is different. Excuse me, I haven't understood you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Yes. Of course. The legal remedies, of course, can be looked into later. All I was asking for is that prior to the next court appearance the parties be informed in advance of that hearing whether or not the Dutch authorities wish to continue with their same treatment of the -- of my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: So obviously prior to the next hearing, we can make a decision as to how to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: I understand. Thank you. Thank you very much. Well, I still recommend the Registrar to take in consideration what has been said by Counsel Khan and try to fit what he is asking for. Well, I think that should be all for the time being. And if nothing else is to be brought about, I'm going to adjourn, not before thanking -- thanking you, the Prosecution, and counsels, and even translator also, of course, and the registrar for your help. And this meeting is adjourned now.
